# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# Expectation for `node_data_dir_single_writer` against input/. See
# tests/fixtures/doctor/node_data_dir_single_writer/expect.json for the NUL-byte warning and the
# canonicalisation trap.
#
# THIS CASE IS THE SECOND HALF OF §2i'S FIRST PROBE, AND THE ONE AN IMPLEMENTER SKIPS. §2i says: read
# /proc/*/cmdline for a monerod "whose --data-dir (OR WHOSE --config-file's data-dir=) resolves to the
# same canonical path". Here argv carries NO --data-dir:
#   /usr/bin/monerod\0--config-file\0/etc/monerod.conf\0--non-interactive\0
# and the data dir is named only inside that conf file. A detector that reads argv alone finds no
# match, reports the data dir FREE, and `node up` starts a SECOND WRITER on a live LMDB (§1.2) -- the
# single failure this whole check exists to prevent. The other two cases both pass such a detector.
#
# THE CONF PATH IN THE cmdline IS /etc/monerod.conf, WHICH THIS FIXTURE CANNOT CREATE (no agent on
# this machine can write /etc, and sudo needs a password -- §1.1). input/monerod.conf holds the bytes;
# the harness must make the detector read them for that path. Two honest ways, and the Phase 2 doctor
# agent picks one and records it:
#   (a) rewrite the cmdline fixture at harness time so --config-file points at input/monerod.conf
#       (it is generated, not hand-written -- see tests/fixtures/README.md), or
#   (b) resolve a conf path through paths.proc_root's parent when FMONERO_PROC_ROOT is set.
# (a) needs no product code and is what Phase 0 recommends: the file is one NUL-joined argv.
# IF NEITHER IS DONE the case cannot run, and it must then be recorded as SKIPPED, never as passing --
# a gate that cannot fail is worse than no gate (§2j).
#
# THE CONF FILE'S OWN CONTENT is upstream's template (utils/conf/monerod.conf:1-8): data-dir,
# log-file, log-level, absolute paths only. boost::program_options reads it, NOT systemd, so there are
# no %h/%S specifiers to expand (src/daemon/command_line_args.h:40-53, applied in
# src/daemon/main.cpp:215-241) -- the same reason units::render_node_conf must emit absolute paths and
# has a permanent unit test saying so (§4.2).
# ARGV WINS OVER THE FILE when both name a data dir: po::store is called on argv first and boost never
# overwrites an already-set value (src/daemon/main.cpp:215-241). So the conf is consulted only when
# argv is silent, which is exactly this case.
# status `fail` and the pid named, as in the base case.
